points.why: It warns against a verdict and against simulating a disputed structure, but never says the problem definition itself is contested and proposes its own framing.

It calls for a picture all four groups recognise, built live with everyone in the room, but treats this as link-drawing rather than surfacing each worldview, and places it after a stock-and-flow sketch.
It never runs CATWOE or examines the worldview behind each group's preferred fix.
It has no consulted/informed/not-consulted marking, and it sketches stock-and-flow in step 2 before any definition is agreed.

pitfalls.why: It explicitly cautions that bed shortage may be a symptom and does not build a capacity model around it.

notes: It frames the question around delayed transfers of medically fit patients (closer to the nurses' and social workers' view) and starts a stock-and-flow sketch before stakeholders agree, which partly contradicts its own advice not to declare a winner.
